nodes.name: audio_pipeline.py
nodes.summary: Audio capture pipeline with ring buffer buffering, Silero VAD-based voice activity detection, wake word detection via Porcupine, and speaker voiceprint extraction using SpeechBrain. Emits voice start/end, wake word, and voiceprint events asynchronously.

nodes.languageNotes: Dual-detector architecture: InsightFace provides facial embeddings for recognition, MediaPipe serves as lightweight fallback. Async capture loop with FPS management.

nodes.name: 2026-05-30-frank-01-system-architecture.md
nodes.summary: Core system architecture specification for the Frank identity-aware desktop assistant. Defines the three-tier architecture (Electron renderer process, Electron main process, Python inference service), process lifecycle and IPC mechanisms, state machine design with multi-person debounce, data flow and multimodal fusion decision logic, ring buffer design, multi-output device routing, component design for all major subsystems, deployment directory structure and startup sequence, and security/privacy model.

nodes.name: 2026-05-30-frank-02-identity-recognition.md
nodes.summary: Identity recognition and fusion system specification detailing the dual-modal (face + voiceprint) parallel fusion architecture. Covers the fusion decision matrix with four confidence levels, adaptive threshold engine with registration baseline recording and runtime penalty factors, five-tier role hierarchy with preemption rules, session identity change detection, multi-person meeting mode, and multi-output device routing based on identity context.

nodes.name: 2026-05-30-frank-03-interaction-model.md
nodes.summary: Interaction model and UI design specification for Frank as an always-listening desktop voice assistant. Defines the real-time audio pipeline with ring buffer, four parallel trigger strategies (sound intensity, wake word detection, wake-free commands, visual intent recognition including gaze/nod/head-shake/hand-wave), trigger fusion logic with a decision matrix, application state machine with eight states, voice interaction feedback chain, compact and expanded UI layout modes, listening mode settings, naming conventions, multi-user support, and privacy/security considerations.

nodes.name: 2026-05-30-frank-04-task-plugin-system.md
nodes.summary: Background task management and skill plugin system specification for Frank. Defines command classification into immediate vs managed tasks with LLM-based routing, managed task lifecycle state machine (seven states), queue scheduling rules with persistence, three-tier error handling strategy (auto-recovery, user-decision-required, non-recoverable), task board UI with progress updates, session recovery with persistent storage, completion notifications via toast and chat panel, skill plugin architecture with manifest.json and prompt.md conventions, plugin execution isolation with resource limits, multi-skill orchestration, and a catalog of built-in skills.

nodes.name: 2026-05-30-frank-05-member-biometrics.md
nodes.summary: Member management and biometric data design specification detailing the complete lifecycle of person data in Frank. Covers the dual identity source model (identified members and unidentified visitors), automatic discovery pipeline with matching thresholds and quality gates, first-interaction auto-tagging rules, owner registration flow with UI guidance, biometric database schema with SQLite storage and security constraints, adaptive embedding update algorithm using weighted moving average, member deletion strategies, unidentified person auto-cleanup with configurable retention, posture/gesture recognition module interface design, fusion scoring calculation, and role-based access control overview.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with README.md to understand the project's core concept: Frank is an identity-aware desktop home assistant built with Electron and Python. The README states the project's bilingual identity and positions Frank as a personal agent that recognizes who you are. This document is the most important first stop because it establishes the project's purpose before any code is examined.

tour.title: Project Scaffold and Architecture
tour.description: The package.json defines the Electron frontend dependencies (Electron v33, electron-builder, ws for WebSocket). Complementing it is the system architecture specification, which documents the three-tier design: Electron renderer process for UI, Electron main process as host, and Python inference service for AI workloads. Together they reveal the project's dual-language architecture and the decision to keep the frontend as vanilla HTML/CSS/JS without frameworks.

tour.title: Electron Main Process
tour.description: The Electron main process entry point (main.js) bootstraps the entire application: it loads YAML configuration via config.js, spawns the Python inference service as a child process, creates the main window and a separate preview window for camera feed, manages system tray integration, and establishes a WebSocket connection to the Python backend with exponential-backoff reconnection. This file is the bridge between the desktop shell and the AI service, making it essential to understand before any feature code.
tour.languageLesson: Electron's main process uses CommonJS require() and manages child processes via child_process.spawn(). The config.js implements a custom YAML parser instead of using an external library, using indentation-level tracking and recursive value parsing for nested keys and lists.

tour.title: IPC Bridge and Preload Security
tour.description: The IPC handler (ipc.js) registers Electron ipcMain.handle channels that bridge the renderer process to the main process and Python backend. It provides state querying, message forwarding, window controls, preview window management, and device toggles. The preload script (preload.js) uses contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld to selectively expose these IPC channels to the renderer, enforcing Electron's context isolation model. This is how the UI communicates with the system without direct access to Node.js APIs.
tour.languageLesson: Electron context isolation prevents the renderer from accessing Node.js or Electron APIs directly. The preload script uses contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld to define a controlled API surface, while ipcMain.handle / ipcRenderer.invoke provide async request-response patterns between processes.

tour.title: Python WebSocket Server
tour.description: The Python server entry point (main.py) is the heart of Frank's AI capabilities. Its main() function initializes and wires together every module: camera pipeline, audio pipeline, identity fusion engine, LLM provider, state machine, role manager, task manager, skill loader, multi-person tracker, pose/gesture detector, and conversation orchestrator. It then starts a WebSocket server and registers event callbacks for face detection, voice activity, identity changes, and gesture events. The handle_message function dispatches over 30 message types to their respective module handlers, making this the central routing hub.
tour.languageLesson: Python asyncio drives the entire server. Module callbacks are wired as async coroutines, and the WebSocket server (from the websockets library) uses async/await throughout. Signal handlers manage graceful shutdown. The handle_message function is a large dispatch table illustrating how a single-server pattern routes typed JSON messages.

tour.title: Shared Configuration and Message Protocol
tour.description: The shared config module (config.py) loads YAML configuration with deep-merge for partial updates, reload support, and sensitive value sanitization. The message module (message.py) defines the typed WebSocket protocol with Message and ErrorMessage data classes, auto-generated IDs, and ISO timestamps. These two files are imported by nearly every module in the Python service, forming the communication and configuration foundation that all downstream code depends on.

tour.title: Camera and Audio Perception Pipelines
tour.description: The camera pipeline (camera_pipeline.py) uses OpenCV with a dual-detector strategy: InsightFace as the primary face detector offering 512-dim facial embeddings, with MediaPipe as a lightweight fallback. It captures frames asynchronously, detects faces, extracts embeddings, emits face detected/lost events, and supports face thumbnail capture. The audio pipeline (audio_pipeline.py) captures microphone input via PyAudio, detects voice activity with Silero VAD, recognizes wake words via Porcupine, and extracts speaker voiceprints using SpeechBrain. These two perception pipelines are the eyes and ears of the assistant, feeding the identity fusion engine with raw biometric evidence.
tour.languageLesson: Both pipelines use asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe to dispatch events from background threads back into the async event loop. The camera pipeline implements a dual-detector architecture: InsightFace for recognition-quality embeddings, MediaPipe for lightweight fallback. The audio pipeline combines Silero VAD (voice activity), Porcupine (wake word), and SpeechBrain (voiceprint) into a single threaded capture loop.

tour.title: Multi-Modal Identity Fusion
tour.description: The identity fusion engine (identity_fusion.py) is the core intelligence that recognizes who is present. It maintains parallel face and voice evidence queues, evaluates combined evidence against configurable thresholds using a fusion decision matrix, and manages identity state transitions (unknown, tentative, confirmed, changing). When both face and voice agree on an identity above threshold, it emits confirmed events; when they conflict, it signals changing or unknown states. The role manager (role_manager.py) assigns a 5-tier role (owner/admin/member/child/guest) to each identified person, enforcing permission checks, session lifecycle management, daily usage limits, and preemption priority. Together, these modules implement Frank's defining feature: identity-aware interaction.
tour.languageLesson: The fusion engine uses a decision matrix with four confidence combination outcomes based on face and voice evidence being high or low. The role system maps to an enum hierarchy with permission checks at each level. Session management creates per-identity contexts with timestamps, usage counters, and preemption rules for concurrent access.

tour.title: Biometric Database and Member Management
tour.description: The database layer (database.py) manages SQLite storage with schema migration support (up to v4), embedding serialization for face and voice vectors, cosine similarity search for biometric matching, and full CRUD operations for members and unidentified persons. The member manager (member_manager.py) provides registration workflows with face and voice sample collection, member CRUD with stats and history queries, automatic discovery and conversion of unidentified visitors, face thumbnail and voiceprint spectrum updates, and privacy-preserving record deletion. This is where biometric data gets persisted and queried during identity recognition.
tour.languageLesson: Face and voice embeddings are serialized as byte blobs using numpy's tobytes() and stored in SQLite BLOB columns. Cosine similarity search iterates over all stored embeddings to find the closest match -- no vector index is used for this local-only database. The database uses WAL journal mode for concurrent reads and foreign keys for referential integrity.

tour.title: State Machine and Conversation Orchestration
tour.description: The hierarchical state machine (state_machine.py) defines Frank's behavioral states: idle, waiting_for_wake, listening, processing, and responding. It manages event-driven transitions, identity tracking, configurable per-state timeouts, a timeout monitor, and state change callbacks. The conversation orchestrator (conversation.py) builds on this by managing the full voice interaction pipeline: receiving wake word events, triggering speech transcription (STT), routing through wake-free command matching, invoking the LLM for responses, and sending the result to TTS for spoken output. It tracks chat sub-states (idle/listening/thinking/speaking) to coordinate the real-time flow.
tour.languageLesson: Python Enum classes define the state hierarchy. The state machine uses a flat transition table approach (not a state pattern class hierarchy), with identity context threaded through each state. The conversation orchestrator implements a pipeline pattern: STT -> LLM -> TTS as sequential async stages with callback hooks at each boundary.

tour.title: Skill Plugin System
tour.description: The skill loader (skill_loader.py) implements an extensible plugin system that discovers Python-based skills from a directory, loads them via manifest.json metadata, executes them in isolated multiprocessing subprocesses with timeouts, and aggregates their prompts for LLM context. It includes a file watcher for hot-reload during development. The built-in reminder skill (handler.py) demonstrates the plugin contract: each skill exports a handle function that receives typed parameters and returns results through a Queue. The manifest.json for each skill defines name, version, permissions, and min_user_level for role-gated access.
tour.languageLesson: Skills run in multiprocessing.Process subprocesses for isolation, with results communicated via multiprocessing.Queue. This prevents a crashing skill from taking down the main server. The loader uses importlib to dynamically discover and load skill modules, with manifest.json providing metadata and prompt.md providing LLM context templates.

tour.title: Desktop UI Shell
tour.description: The main renderer script (app.js) provides the entire frontend experience: a PanelManager for slide-over panels (identity, member management, settings, persona, task detail, registration wizard), chat overlay with message streaming, notification system, gesture UI feedback, and device status indicators. It subscribes to all IPC events from the preload bridge and renders DOM elements accordingly. The index.html defines the main window structure with three zones: status bar at top, orb/tasks area in the middle, and bottom navigation bar. The UI is built entirely with vanilla JavaScript and CSS -- no React, Vue, or other framework -- keeping the frontend lightweight and directly coupled to the IPC event model.
tour.languageLesson: The renderer uses vanilla JavaScript DOM manipulation with a PanelManager singleton managing overlay lifecycle. Event-driven rendering means all UI updates come through IPC subscriptions (window.electronAPI.on*). The navigateTo() pattern switches between full-window views by manipulating the currentView state variable, gating DOM rendering for inactive views to reduce overhead.
